A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ALIGNVLM research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support matching retained, relocated and revised content.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, connector comparisons, noise experiments, VCR results and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds low-resource evaluations, vocabulary-restriction results, embedding analysis and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The main architecture, LM-head initialization and probability-weighted text embedding connector remain unchanged. Section 5.3 adds a limited, evaluation-only inference variant retaining approximately 3.4K embeddings instead of the full 128K vocabulary; this does not replace the main connector.

E1.justification: v2 adds training on LLaVA-558K and LLaVA-NeXT-779K and evaluates general vision-language capabilities on MMMU-dev, SeedBench, MMVet, POPE and GQA. This substantially extends coverage beyond document-focused evaluation. The original document benchmarks and VCR remain; the small, manually curated word-crop probe from v1 Appendix A.2 is removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B, InternVL-3-2B/8B and Fuyu-8B while retaining the original comparators. The new low-resource comparison additionally evaluates H-Reducer (1×4) and HoneyBee (C-Abstractor) alongside MLP, Perceiver and Ovis, substantially broadening the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: Section 5.2.2 introduces a separate two-stage low-resource protocol with connector-only pretraining, subsequent component-specific learning rates, new image-resolution settings and smaller training budgets. Additional protocols include restricted-vocabulary evaluation, 2,500-sample runtime measurements and cosine-distance measurement under noise. The original three-stage hyperparameters and retained benchmark splits are unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds low-resource connector analysis, PCA and vocabulary-restriction experiments, runtime/memory comparisons, and embedding-distance evidence for noise robustness. It removes v1's word-crop token-decoding analysis and Figure 6. The VCR experiment, its failure examples and the other document case studies are retained, with VCR relocated to Appendix A.3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, run-to-run variability or formal significance tests. The additional results remain point estimates; average runtime reporting does not establish uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Matched values in Tables 1–2, VCR results and noise-related accuracy drops are unchanged. v2 adds substantial results: ALIGN averages 59.32 on document tasks and 56.88 on general tasks in the new low-resource regime; restricted-vocabulary evaluation yields 58.69 versus 58.81 with full embeddings. It also adds baseline scores, runtime measurements and noise cosine distances of 0.0036 for ALIGN versus 0.3938 for MLP. These are additional experimental results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The connector equations, convex-hull argument and mathematical comparisons with MLP and visual embedding tables are retained. The new PCA, pruning and distance analyses provide empirical evidence rather than new definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The central ALIGN contribution remains. v2 adds explicit claims of data efficiency, faster convergence and larger gains under low-resource training. Its conclusion narrows the claim about open-source instructed models from outperforming them to achieving competitive performance.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantial interpretations concerning efficient learning from linguistic priors, suitability for resource-constrained settings, compact vocabulary coverage and potential pruning. Appendix A.2 explains why the extra LM head allegedly adds little computational overhead. The detailed punctuation/whitespace mechanism discussion is removed, while the VCR proper-name failure interpretation is preserved.

D1.justification: v2 documents the additional training recipe through learning rates, batch sizes, epochs, frozen components, GPU count, resolution and token counts. It explicitly clarifies shared settings for the existing connector comparison. The future code-release promise becomes a stated code/artifact release with a project address. Original three-stage hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds convolution-based connectors as an explicit category, discussing HoneyBee, H-Reducer and ResNet. References expand to newer Qwen2.5-VL and InternVL3 models and the added general-vision benchmarks. The overall deep/shallow-fusion framing and positioning against MLP and Ovis remain.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted revisions to the title, abstract, introduction and result interpretations while retaining much of the original prose and section sequence. Section 5.2 is divided into high- and low-resource regimes, VCR moves to the appendix, and the Impact Statement is removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column format to a predominantly single-column layout. v2 adds low-resource, vocabulary-restriction and runtime tables plus a PCA figure, expands Table 1, removes the visual-to-token grid figure, and resizes or relocates existing displays, including the VCR figures.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for applicability and practical efficiency through controlled low-resource comparisons, general-vision evaluations, broader baselines, vocabulary ablation and runtime measurements—important gaps in v1's empirical support. These benefits outweigh removal of the word-crop diagnostic and a localized new reporting error: Fuyu-8B's nine Table 1 scores average approximately 27.98, not the reported 22.97. The faster-convergence claim still lacks direct convergence evidence.
